title: On-Prem Inference Vendor Responsibilities & Evidence Matrix
content:
Purpose and context

This working draft defines a responsibility matrix and minimal evidence checklist intended to be bundled with contractual terms for vendors who operate or install on-prem inference components (appliances, air-gapped packages, or VPC-hosted private nodes). The goal is to make negotiation faster by aligning security, operational, and legal expectations up front, and to reduce back-and-forth on evidence requests during procurement.

Scope

- Applies to third-party vendors and integrators that will deploy inference-capable software or hardware into customer-managed environments where Redwood claims any support, SLA, or managed-service obligations.
- Covers controls related to access, deployment, data handling, cryptographic keys, patching, forensics, and decommissioning.
- Excludes typical SaaS-hosted relationships (those are covered under hosted API templates).

How to use this file

- Use the matrix as an appendix to the supplier security addendum or as an exhibit to the DPA for on-prem engagements.
- For each control area, the matrix indicates the primary responsible party, secondary/assist role, the typical form of evidence required, and minimum frequency for evidence refresh.
- Negotiation notes and sample contract language are provided at the end for quick insertion into customer agreements.

Responsibility matrix (text table)

Control area | Primary responsible | Secondary/assist | Evidence required | Refresh frequency
- Access control and privileged access management | Vendor for local agent; Customer for environment accounts | Redwood support (access during debug) | Access list, just-in-time access logs, RBAC config snippets, proof of JIT tooling | On install, then annually or after major upgrade
- Data residency and storage encryption at rest | Customer (owns keys) for data storage; Vendor for software storage of cached artifacts | Redwood for cache-handling guidance | KMS key policy excerpt, disk encryption config, KV cache eviction/TTL settings | On install and each major version change
- Transit encryption and mTLS for control plane | Vendor must implement TLS; Customer to supply trust anchors and cert signing process | Redwood to verify during onboarding | TLS config dump, certificate chain, cipher list, mTLS proof-of-concept call logs | On install and after cert rotation
- Key management and HSM/KMS integration | Customer-managed keys recommended; vendor to support HSM/HSM proxies | Redwood to document integration steps | Integration how-to, test vector signature logs, KMS audit record excerpt (redacted) | Demonstration during onboarding and annually
- Vulnerability management and patch rollout | Vendor responsible for signed updates and patch notes; Customer schedules patch windows | Redwood to provide compatibility notes and rollout guidance | Signed release manifest, CVE reconciliations for included components, rollback plan | Per release and quarterly reconciliations
- Telemetry and telemetry minimization | Vendor to implement local telemetry controls; Customer to configure export policies | Redwood to recommend minimal telemetry for support | Telemetry schema, sampling config, proof of no PII retained in local telemetry, diagram of flow | On install and after config changes
- Forensics and incident evidence preservation | Vendor to support artifact collection APIs; Customer to preserve chain of custody | Redwood incident team to coordinate evidence requests | Forensic collection procedure, sample artifacts (hashes), SLA for handing files to customer/legal | On demand; tabletop annually
- Secure decommissioning and data erasure | Customer to trigger decommission; Vendor to provide erasure tools and attestation | Redwood to provide checklist templates | Erasure runbook, erasure attestation signed by vendor, wipe logs | At decommission

Minimum evidence standards (plain language)

- All evidence must be time-stamped, verifiable (signed or checksummed), and contain minimal necessary context to prove the control without leaking customer data.
- Where logs or artifacts contain customer-specific content, vendor must provide redacted extracts plus checksum of full artifact held by customer.
- Evidence provided as screenshots is acceptable for low-sensitivity items but not for cryptographic proofs or audit logs.

Sample contract clauses (editable snippets)

1) Evidence delivery clause (to include in security addendum)
Vendor will deliver, within 10 business days of written request, the artifacts and supporting materials identified in the On-Prem Inference Vendor Responsibilities & Evidence Matrix as held by Vendor. Vendor may redact customer-specific content where necessary but must provide checksums and a redacted index sufficient to validate the scope of the artifacts delivered.

2) Joint incident response clause
In the event of a security incident affecting the deployed components, Parties will follow the Joint Incident Response Plan. Vendor will preserve and make available forensic artifacts for 90 days or longer if required by applicable law or legal hold. Vendor will follow Customer instructions for evidence export and will not delete or alter preserved artifacts.

Negotiation and risk notes (internal)

- Customers often push for vendor-supplied KMS; push back strongly: default should be customer-managed keys with vendor proving integration. Exceptions require strict contract language and escrow terms for keys.
- Be prepared to accept redacted telemetry extracts rather than full logs when customers require high confidentiality; establish sampling and checksum approach ahead of time to avoid last-minute stalls.
- Avoid blanket warranties around absolute erasure unless vendor can provide hardware-level wipe guarantees and signed attestation. For appliances, require physical decommission proof.

Open questions and items to resolve before finalizing template

- Acceptable forms of signed attestation for decommissioning (not all vendors will use HSM-backed signing). Confirm legal team preference.
- Minimum retention of evidence for compliance customers (some regulators will require longer than 90 days).
- Standard redaction policy template to include with evidence deliveries.

Next steps and owners

- Review with Legal (Marcus Lee): confirm attestation language and limits for indemnity (owner: Marcus Lee, due 2025-11-17).
- Run this matrix by Solutions Engineering (Sofia Martinez) for operational feasibility notes on the evidence formats (owner: Sofia Martinez, due 2025-11-10).
- Prototype evidence packet (sample files, checksums) for one pilot vendor and validate redaction approach (owner: Ethan Zhao, due 2025-12-05).

Appendix: quick checklist for onboarding package

- Signed installation manifest and manifest signature
- TLS certificate chain and mTLS test call log
- KMS integration test vector and audit snippet (redacted)
- Telemetry sampling config and schema document
- Patch/upgrade policy and rollback checklist
- Data erasure runbook and attestation template

Notes to self and rough edits

- Need to add small diagram for data flow; will add to Confluence page CONFLUENCE-1234 and link here.
- Consider adding short clause on third-party subprocessor use by vendor for component supply chains.

End of working draft

Feedback welcome. This is intended to be pragmatic and negotiable - prioritize demonstrable artifacts over perfect wording during early pilots.
